back: Reducing the number of employees, usually to cut costs or because less work is needed.
Losing a job because the job is no longer needed, through no fault of the employee.
Redundancy: the job has gone, not the worker's fault, usually with a payment. Dismissal: due to conduct or ability.
Automation, fall in demand, cost cutting, reorganisation, closure or relocation, merger.
Natural wastage, voluntary redundancy or early retirement, part-time hours, retraining and redeployment.

front: Fair criteria for choosing who to make redundant?
back: Skills, performance, attendance and discipline, length of service; applied equally, never discriminatory.

front: Effects of downsizing on remaining staff?
back: Fear for job security, heavier workloads, lower morale unless well communicated.
Letting the workforce fall by not replacing employees who leave or retire.
